research_question: How do loss regularization, structural perturbation severity, and adaptive loss weighting affect cross-modality representation invariance and calibration across CNN, Transformer, and Foundation architectures?

hypotheses.H1_regularization: High label smoothing (α=0.12) significantly reduces calibration error (ECE) by discouraging overconfident posterior margins.
hypotheses.H2_structural_invariance: Aggressive contour erasing and affine shearing force macro-geometric learning, lifting worst-case accuracy on broken-line variants.
hypotheses.H3_curriculum_weighting: Adaptive 2.0x loss weighting on empirically diagnosed fragile modalities yields the highest overall Pareto accuracy and lowest flip rate.

conditions.name: Config_1_Standard_Baseline
conditions.description: Standard label-smoothed cross-entropy with moderate contour erasing and mild affine shear.

conditions.name: Config_2_High_Regularization
conditions.description: High label smoothing (α=0.12) and elevated temperature scaling (T=1.35) to maximize entropy regularization.

conditions.name: Config_3_Aggressive_Augmentation
conditions.description: Aggressive contour disruption with heavy erasing cutouts and extreme shear to force macro-shape invariance.

conditions.name: Config_4_Adaptive_Fragility_Weighted
conditions.description: Curriculum feedback: upweights fragile representations (Dotted, Dashed, Sketch, Silhouette) by 2.0x in loss.
